==English== ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:devis>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|devis}}, {{m|enm|devise}}, {{m|enm|devyce}}, {{m|enm|devys}}, {{m|enm|devyse}}, from {{der|en|fro|devis}} and {{m|fro|devise}},{{R:MED Online|entry=dēvīs|pos=n|id=MED11478}} from {{der|en|la|dīvīsus}}, past participle of {{m|la|dīvidō||to divide}}. {{doublet|en|devise#Noun|pos1=noun}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/dɪˈvaɪs/|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/dɪˈvaɪs/|a=GA,CA}} * {{IPA|en|[dɪˈvʌɪs]|a=Canadian raising}} ** {{IPA|en|/dəˈvaɪs/|a=weak vowel}} * {{audio|en|en-us-device.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/dɪˈvɑɪs/|a=AU}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪs|s=2}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # Any piece of [[equipment]] made for a particular purpose, especially a mechanical or electrical one. #: {{nearsyn|en|equipment#Noun|tool|machine}} #* {{RQ:Economist|title=A better waterworks|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|issue=8838 |page=5 (Technology Quarterly) |url=http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21578526-medical-technology-artificial-kidneys-are-getting-closer-becoming-clinical |passage=An artificial kidney these days still means a refrigerator-sized dialysis machine. Such '''devices''' mimic the way real kidneys cleanse blood and eject impurities and surplus water as urine.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625180618/http://www.economist.com:80/news/technology-quarterly/21578526-medical-technology-artificial-kidneys-are-getting-closer-becoming-clinical|archivedate=25 June 2017}} # {{lb|en|computer hardware}} A [[peripheral device]]; an item of [[hardware]]. # A [[project]] or [[scheme]], often designed to deceive; a [[stratagem]]; an [[artifice]]. 1602, Shakespeare, ''The Merry Wives of Windsor. "''This is our device,/ That Falstaff at that oak shall meet with us." #* {{RQ:King James Version|Jeremiah|51|11|passage=His '''device''' is against Babylon, to destroy it.}} #* {{RQ:King James Version|Job|5|12|passage=He disappointeth the '''devices''' of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1827|author=Henry Hallam|title=s:The English Constitution|publisher=Harper |passage=Their recent '''device''' of demanding benevolences.}} #* {{RQ:London Sea-Wolf|30|passage=So next day the hunting began. I did not know how to shoot, but I proceeded to learn. And when I had expended some thirty shells for three seals, I decided that the ammunition would be exhausted before I acquired the necessary knowledge. I had used eight shells for lighting fires before I hit upon the '''device''' of banking the embers with wet moss, and there remained not over a hundred shells in the box.}} #* {{RQ:Burroughs Return of Tarzan|version=Burt|page=58|passage=FOR a month Tarzan was a regular and very welcome devotee at the shrine of the beautiful Countess de Coude. {{...}} More often Olga found '''devices''' that would give her an hour of Tarzan alone.}} # {{lb|en|Ireland}} An [[improvised explosive device]], home-made [[bomb]] #* {{quote-song|en|year=1979|author=Stiff Little Fingers|title=Suspect '''Device''' |passage=Inflammable material is planted in my head / It's a suspect '''device''' that's left 2000 dead}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=September 3 2014|author=Cliodhna Russell|journal=The Journal|titleurl=http://www.thejournal.ie/army-bomb-disposal-cavan-1652559-Sep2014/|title=A viable '''device''' was found in Cavan today, it has now been made safe |passage=THE ARMY BOMB Disposal Team rendered safe a viable '''device''' in Cavan this afternoon.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251105121755/https://www.thejournal.ie/army-bomb-disposal-cavan-1652559-Sep2014/|archivedate=5 November 2025}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=August 3 2014|author=Louise Kelly; Conor Feehan|title=Suspect '''device''' found at shopping centre revealed as hoax|titleurl=http://www.independent.ie/irish-news/news/suspect-device-found-at-shopping-centre-revealed-as-hoax-30480191.html|journal=Irish Independent |passage=The army bomb squad carried out two controlled explosions on the '''device'''. It was later found that the suspect '''device''' was a hoax and not a viable explosive.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221101165030/https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/news/suspect-device-found-at-shopping-centre-revealed-as-hoax-30480191.html|archivedate=1 November 2022}} # {{lb|en|rhetoric}} A technique that an author or speaker uses to evoke an emotional response in the audience; a [[rhetorical]] '''device'''.{{senseid|en|heraldry}}{{lb|en|heraldry}} A [[motto]], [[emblem]], or other mark used to distinguish the bearer from others. A device differs from a [[badge]] or [[cognizance]] primarily as it is a personal distinction, and not a badge borne by members of the same house successively. # {{lb|en|archaic}} Power of [[devising]]; invention; contrivance. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1824|author=Walter Savage Landor|chapter=King Henry IV and Sir Arnold Savage|title=Imaginary Conversations of Literary Men and Statesmen|page=44 |passage=Moreover I must have instruments of mine own '''device''', weighty, and exceeding costly}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=1976|author=The Eagles|title=Hotel California |passage=And she said,
"We are all prisoners here,
Of our own '''device'''"}} # {{lb|en|legal}} An image used in whole or in part as a [[trademark]] or service mark. # {{lb|en|printing}} An image or logo denoting official or proprietary authority or provenience. # {{lb|en|crosswording}} Any specific class of [[wordplay]] element in a [[cryptic crossword]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2001|month=06|author=Fraser Simpson|title=101 Cryptic Crosswords: From the New Yorker|publisher=Sterling Publishing Company, Inc.|isbn=9780806901862|page=6 |text=These eight '''devices''', and combinations thereof, account for nearly every kind of wordplay you will encounter in cryptic crosswords.}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=2013-11-07|author=Alan Connor|title=Two Girls, One on Each Knee: The Puzzling, Playful World of the Crossword|publisher=Penguin UK|isbn=9780141977119 |text=Discovering these variants is much of the fun. All the '''devices''' can be combined and twisted to produce surface readings in each clue which point you in the wrong direction.}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=2020-03-30|author=Denise Sutherland|title=Solving Cryptic Crosswords For Dummies|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=9780730384700|page=48 |text=As with all varieties of cryptic clues, the container '''device''' can be used in conjunction with other '''devices''', especially in more complex cryptic crosswords.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} A spectacle or [[show]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1634|author={{w|James Shirley}} (falsely attributed to {{w|John Fletcher}})|title=[[w:The Coronation (play)|The Coronation]]|passage=It will be out of faſhion to weare ſwords, / Maſques, and '''devices''' welcome, I ſalute you {{...}}}} #
